newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian 266-day bills yield 33.22 percent vs 37.05.
newsitem.headline: Russian 266-day bills yield 33.22 percent vs 37.05.

text.p: The annualised average yield on an issue of 266-day GKO discount Treasury bills was 33.22 percent at an auction on Wednesday, after 37.05 percent at the last auction of 266-day paper on January 8, the Central Bank said.
The series 22067 bills maturing October 1, the closest in outstanding maturity to the new paper, closed on Tuesday with a yield of 33.66 percent.
Issue volume 7.50 trln rbls 7.50 trln rbls
The Finance Ministry is also selling a new 3.00 trillion rouble tranche of the 18-month OFZ interest-bearing government bond maturing June 17, 1998, (series 24010) on Wednesday.

On January 15 the Finance Ministry is also repaying about 6.08 trillion roubles of maturing six-month bills (series 22039), and paying about 582 billion roubles in interest on the two-year OFZ bond (series 24008) maturing July 1998.
The new bills are subject to the existing tax regime, which frees income from government securities from tax.

President Boris Yeltsin signed a law on Wednesday imposing a 15 percent tax on income from government securities but it has not yet come into force. Securities issued before the tax comes into effect will not be taxable.
